results.summary_before: Redco is a reconfigurable digitally controlled oscillator built from a five-inverter ring oscillator feeding a flip-flop clock divider. It can be used as a ring oscillator by shorting out0 back to the input, or as a clock divider and DCO selected by three binary control pins, with outputs on out0 and out1. The documentation explains the pin functions and configuration but the project is a Wokwi design with no tiles and no measured silicon results. No external hardware is specified.
results.summary: Redco is a reconfigurable digitally controlled oscillator built from a five-inverter ring oscillator feeding a flip-flop clock divider. It can be used as a ring oscillator by shorting out0 to in0 and in4, or as a clock divider/DCO selected by three binary control pins, with outputs on out0 and out1. The documentation explains the pin functions and configuration; it is a Wokwi design with no tiles, no measured silicon results, and no external hardware specified. The frequency is described as 1/(5*inverter cell delay) for the ring oscillator case.

results.summary_before: This is a 32-bit RISC-V IMA SoC capable of booting Linux, featuring external SPI flash and PSRAM, a UART, and a SPI peripheral. It is tested by building a system image and loading it into the SPI flash, then running at 30 MHz (max tested 34.5 MHz). External hardware includes a QSPI Pmod for flash and PSRAM, and a UART connection for communication. Notable for being a full Linux-capable SoC on a Tiny Tapeout chip.
results.summary: This is a 32-bit RISC-V IMA SoC capable of booting Linux, featuring external SPI flash and PSRAM, a UART, and a SPI peripheral. It is tested by building a system image and loading it into the SPI flash, then running at 30 MHz (max tested 34.5 MHz). External hardware includes a QSPI Pmod for flash and PSRAM, plus UART over the demo board USB. It is a full Linux-capable SoC implemented in Verilog on a 8x2 tile Tiny Tapeout chip.

results.summary_before: This design is a stylish ring oscillator built from 21 SkullFET inverters, generating a square wave with a simulated frequency of about 169.2 MHz. It is tested by connecting an oscilloscope to the divided outputs, as the full-speed outputs are too fast for GPIO pins. No external hardware is required beyond an oscilloscope. Notable for its use of SkullFET transistors and the inclusion of frequency dividers for observability.
results.summary: This design is a stylish ring oscillator built from 21 SkullFET inverters, generating a square wave with a simulated frequency of about 169.2 MHz. Notable for its use of SkullFET transistors and the inclusion of frequency dividers for observability.
